NFA-A: after the rate test stepped down from 1C to 0.1C[1], it recovered a capacity of ≈170 mAh g^− 1[2], against an initial capacity at 0.1C[3] before the rate tests of ≈184 mAh g^− 1[4]. The paper describes this recovered value as similar to the initial value, with a difference of ≈5%[5]. Checking against the capacities the paper quotes, the gap between them is visibly bigger than that stated difference, so the stated figure should be read with caution.

NFA-F: after the same step down, it delivered only ≈138 mAh g^− 1[6] when compared with its initial capacity of ≈190 mAh g^− 1[7], which the paper reports as a ≈27% loss[8]. The paper concludes that NFA-A was the most stable of the variants tested under these conditions.
